literal: With every intoxication, drinking liquor is like desiring; love, every time it becomes public, is sweet.
translation: Just as drinking liquor is desired more and more as one's intoxication grows, so does love become sweeter and sweeter each time it is revealed to the public.
modern: மதுவினால் மயக்கம் அதிகமாகும் போதெல்லாம் மேலும் மது குடிக்க விரும்புவதைப் போல, காமம் பிறருக்குத் தெரியவரும் போதெல்லாம் மேலும் இன்பம் தருகிறது.
explanation: This couplet compares the nature of secret love to the addiction of drinking liquor. Normally, lovers might fear their secret affair being exposed to the town, but here they find that public gossip only intensifies their passion. The key word 'களித்தொறும்' means 'with every increasing intoxication', and 'வெளிப்படுந்தொறும்' means 'with every public revelation'. Just as an intoxicated person craves more alcohol with every sip, the lovers find their mutual desire growing sweeter and more irresistible every time their love is talked about.
